trip.title: Switzerland
assumptions: Every traveller holds a Swiss Half Fare Card (CHF 150 each, valid one calendar month, bought to cover 4-13 September).
Flights are booked. Four land at Zurich on Friday 4 September at 20:30, the fifth on Saturday 5 September at 06:30, and all five leave for Tel Aviv on Sunday 13 September at 11:45.

Van collected Sunday 6 September morning and returned Saturday 12 September evening - six days, not seven, because the first two days are spent in Zurich without one. Worth asking whether a full week still prices lower.
Accommodation figures are indicative ranges from published rates, except the two airport stays, which are live quotes read on 20 August 2026.
At five people a 7-seat MPV works: the back row folds flat for luggage. At six it would not have.
Fares are the operators' published 2026 tariffs, read in August 2026 from Jungfraubahnen, Männlichen, Schilthornbahn, Rigi Bahnen and SGV.

trip_wide_costs.note: The CHF 509 quote plus a second driver, now over six days rather than seven. Left at the seven-day figure until the shorter hire is quoted.
Vignette already fitted on Swiss rentals. At CHF 1.97 a litre this leaves room to spare.

trip_wide_costs.item: Food beyond the two big shops
trip_wide_costs.note: Self-catered breakfasts and lunches, four dinners out for five at Swiss restaurant prices, and one more day than the plan first carried. Parking at Weggis, Lungern, Stechelberg and the first airport night is costed on the day; Grindelwald comes with the apartment.

days.title: Land at Zurich, sleep in Kloten
days.sleep: Kloten (Allegra Lodge, one two-bedroom suite, night 1 of 2)
days.movement: Land at 20:30. Passport control and bags, then the hotel's shuttle into Kloten, about ten minutes. No van tonight - it is not needed until Sunday.

group.item: Allegra Lodge, two-bedroom suite, night 1 of 2

tips: Only four beds are needed tonight. The fifth traveller lands at 06:30 tomorrow.

No van for the first two days. The rest day is spent in Zurich on foot and by train, which means the hire starts on Sunday and runs six days rather than eight - and nobody drives on the evening they land.
Take the free-cancellation rate and tell the hotel the flight lands at 20:30. There is a self check-in station and a mobile key, so nobody has to be at a desk.
Skip the CHF 25 breakfast on the first morning. Take it on the second, when there is nowhere to be.

days.title: A day in Zurich to land properly
days.movement: Back to the airport for the 06:30 arrival - allow until about 07:15 for passport control and bags. Then the train into the city, 13 minutes from the airport station, and the rest of the day on foot. No van and no driving.
days.parents: Lindenhof for the view over the roofs, the Fraumünster windows, and the lake promenade. All of it flat and paved, with somewhere to sit every hundred metres.
days.adults: Add the Grossmünster tower, the lanes behind Niederdorf, and a swim off one of the lake badis if the weather holds.

group.item: Allegra Lodge, two-bedroom suite, night 2 of 2
Allegra Lodge, single room for the fifth traveller

tips: The fifth traveller lands at 06:30 off an overnight flight. This is the day for that, not a mountain.
Zurich is one hour behind Tel Aviv in September, so there is no jet lag to fight - only the flights themselves.
The shops inside Zurich main station open on Sundays, which almost nothing else in Switzerland does. Worth knowing tomorrow.
If everyone is up to it, the Rhine Falls are 50 minutes direct from the main station and run hourly. If they are not, the lake and the old town are plenty.

days.title: Collect the van and cross to Grindelwald, by way of Lungern
days.movement: Rental Centre, Level 1 of the Airport Center, from 06:00. Then A4 and A14 past Lucerne, A8 over the Brünig through Sarnen and Giswil. At Lungern leave the main road for the old Brünigstrasse along the lake, rejoin at Lungern Süd, then Meiringen, the north shore of Lake Brienz, Interlaken, Wilderswil, Zweilütschinen, Grindelwald.
days.parents: An hour at Lungern: the lakeside path at Obsee is flat and paved, with a restaurant at each end. Then the Pfingstegg terrace and restaurant, five minutes up by cable car.
days.adults: Lungern and the lake, then Pfingstegg plus the Fly-Line or the summer toboggan at CHF 8 a run, or on toward Berghaus Bäregg.
tips: Coop Grindelwald on Dorfstrasse is open 08:00-19:00 every day including Sundays, which is the whole reason a Sunday transfer works.
Take the north-shore road along Lake Brienz rather than the tunnels.
There is no free parking in Grindelwald - insist on an included space when booking.
Lungern has a 3.5 km bypass tunnel. Follow the main road and you pass under the mountain and see nothing - take the old lakeside road, in at Lungern Nord and out at Lungern Süd.

days.title: Männlichen and the Panorama Trail
days.movement: Walk or local bus 121 (free on the guest card) to Grindelwald Terminal, Männlichen gondola 19-25 min. Return by cog train from Kleine Scheidegg. No driving.
days.parents: Panorama Trail Männlichen to Kleine Scheidegg: 4.9 km, 200 m downhill, about 90 minutes, officially rated easy and suitable for all ages and ability levels.
days.adults: Royal Walk to the true summit first (1 km, 15 min, steep), then the Panorama Trail, then on past Kleine Scheidegg to Wengernalp and Wengen.

per_person.item: Männlichen Panorama round trip: gondola up, cog train down

tips: The best day of the trip for the group as a whole.
Fallback if they would rather not walk: gondola back down and spend the afternoon on the flat paved Lauterbrunnen valley floor, bus 141 back every half hour.
Ask for the Panoramaweg round trip to Grindelwald Grund. Bought as a return the gondola costs CHF 17 more each, for a ride down you never take.

days.title: Jungfraujoch - Top of Europe
days.movement: Grindelwald Terminal, Eiger Express gondola to Eigergletscher (15 min), cog railway through the Eiger to Jungfraujoch (26-30 min). About 50 min each way. First departure around 08:00.
days.parents: Sphinx observatory by lift, Ice Palace, the Plateau. Ninety minutes to two hours is plenty at this height, then straight back down.
days.adults: Get off at Eigergletscher on the descent and walk the Eiger Trail to Alpiglen: 6.5 km, about 2.5 hours, mostly descending along the base of the Eiger north face. Train back from Alpiglen.

per_person.item: Jungfraujoch return from Grindelwald, half fare

group.item: Eiger Trail return leg, three adults

tips: THIS DAY FLOATS. Check the summit webcams at breakfast and go on the clearest morning.
September averages a high of 1 C and a low of minus 5 C at the top, before the wind. Coats, hats, gloves, sunglasses, sunscreen.
The final half-hour of the ascent is inside a tunnel with no view.
Do NOT buy the Good Morning Ticket - it cannot be combined with a Half Fare Card.

3,454 m. About half of adults get a headache, dizziness or no appetite up here, and it usually starts two to twelve hours in - which is exactly why a short visit is the plan. Move slowly, drink water, skip the alcohol, take the lift.
Anyone with a heart or lung condition, sleep apnoea, or on medication for either should ask their doctor before the trip, not on the platform. There is a staffed medical room with oxygen at the top.

days.title: Schilthorn, Piz Gloria and Mürren
days.movement: Drive Grindelwald to Stechelberg, 22 km, about 30 min. Park at the Schilthornbahn, CHF 11 for the day, open-air, no height limit. Descend a different way: Mürren, Grütschalp, Lauterbrunnen, then bus 141 back to the van.
days.parents: Summit, brunch at the revolving Piz Gloria, Bond World and Skyline Walk (both free). Then Mürren and the easy Mürren to Winteregg path, 1.5 km on level gravel with a restaurant and a station at the end.
days.adults: Stop at Birg for the Thrill Walk - 200 m of grating, glass floor and rope crossing bolted to the cliff, free. Then the full Grütschalp-Mürren panorama trail or the Northface Trail from Allmendhubel.

per_person.item: Schilthorn round trip via Grütschalp, half fare
Bus 141 Lauterbrunnen to Stechelberg, half fare

tips: Take one of the first cable cars: at the summit for 07:55, 08:25 or 08:45.
Book Piz Gloria for five. It revolves once every 45 minutes, brunch is served to 14:00, and a table reservation is required rather than advisable.
Ask for the round trip via Grütschalp, not a Stechelberg return. Both are CHF 115, but only the round trip covers coming down through Mürren and Lauterbrunnen.
Last cable car off the summit is 17:50. Mürren to Lauterbrunnen runs until 19:58 and bus 141 back to the van at Stechelberg until 23:29, so there is no rush.

days.title: The Aare Gorge, over the Brünig, and Lucerne at dusk
days.movement: Grindelwald to Meiringen, about 30 minutes, for the gorge. Then back over the Brünig through Giswil and Sarnen, A8 and A2 to Hergiswil, and along the lake to Weggis. About two hours' driving plus the gorge. In the evening, the boat across to Lucerne and back.
days.parents: Aare Gorge from the west entrance - smaller wheelchairs and narrow pushchairs manage to mid-gorge. Then the boat into Lucerne for the Chapel Bridge, the Lion Monument and a flat Old Town.
days.adults: Full 1.4 km of the gorge walkway, about an hour. In Lucerne, add the Musegg Wall towers, which involve stairs.
tips: See the Chapel Bridge early evening, not midday. That is exactly what this day is shaped around.
The last boat back from Lucerne leaves at 19:12 and reaches Weggis at 19:53. After that it is bus 502 by way of the train, about 50 minutes.
The Jungfrau Region guest card takes 20% off a single entry to the gorge. Ask at the desk whether it still counts on your checkout day.
If the gorge and the drive have been enough, the boat slides to tomorrow evening after Rigi. Nothing here is booked.

days.title: Mount Rigi
days.movement: Walk to the Weggis cable-car station in the village. Van stays parked.
days.parents: Cable car to Kaltbad, cogwheel to Rigi Kulm. Paved summit paths with a marked easier route. Kanzeli viewpoint from Kaltbad is about an hour, gentle.
days.adults: Rigi Panorama Trail, Kulm to Kaltbad: 6 km, 1h45, wide gravel, mostly downhill.
tips: Buy the Day Pass - same price as a single return but covers every train and cable car on the mountain.
Bring a picnic. Summit food is the most common complaint about Rigi.
Rain plan: boat to Flüelen and back by train, about CHF 27 half fare, three hours, no walking.

First cable car up from Weggis is around 08:10 and then every half hour, but check the board on the day - the timetable is not the same on a weekday as on a Sunday. The cogwheel from Kaltbad to Kulm runs hourly, so plan around that.

days.title: Back to Zurich, and the Knabenschiessen
days.movement: An easy morning in Weggis, then along the lake to Küssnacht am Rigi and A4 north past Zug to Kloten. About an hour. Refuel in town, drop the van at the airport - Parking 3 takes returns around the clock - and take the hotel shuttle. The evening is the festival.
days.parents: The Knabenschiessen at Albisgütli: a funfair, food stalls and most of the city out. Flat ground, and you can leave whenever you like.
days.adults: Same, and stay late - it runs until 01:30 and the trains keep going well past midnight.

group.item: Allegra Lodge, family room sleeping five

tips: The Knabenschiessen is Zurich's own festival, 12 to 14 September, and Saturday is the opening day. Free to walk into, and it runs until 01:30.
Tram 13 normally ends at Albisgütli, but during the festival it stops at Laubegg, four minutes short. There is no visitor parking at all, which is one more reason the van goes back first.
Refuel before the airport, not on the way to it. Rental is full-to-full, and a motorway services charges the worst prices in the country.
One family room sleeps all five for CHF 279. If five in one room on the last night is too close for comfort, a double and a triple at the Welcome Inn is CHF 377.

days.title: Late morning flight home
days.movement: The hotel's free shuttle to the terminal. No van to return - it went back yesterday.
tips: Be at the terminal by 08:45 for the 11:45 departure. Flights to Tel Aviv carry extra security interviews, and Zurich asks three hours for them rather than two.
Check-in opens at 04:00 at the earliest, so there is nothing to gain by going before those three hours.

weather_swaps.do: Swap the day entirely. The only thing here ruined by weather, and the most expensive ticket.
Boat to Flüelen and back by train. Three hours through the dramatic far end of the lake, seated, no walking.
Grindelwald First. Cliff Walk free with the gondola. Adventure Package CHF 81 reduced adds carts and trottibikes. Skip the First Flyer and Glider - 2-3 hour queues reported.
Harder Kulm. Ten-minute funicular from Interlaken, flat at the top, classic two-lakes view. Most accessible summit in the region.
Schynige Platte. Vintage cog railway, free alpine garden with 750+ species, notably quieter than the famous peaks.
Trümmelbach Falls. Ten glacier falls inside the mountain, but stairs beyond the halfway lift and permanently wet - adults only.

weather_swaps.instead_of: A clear morning on the Brünig
weather_swaps.do: Lungern-Turren. Ten minutes by cable car from Lungern-Obsee to a terrace facing the Bernese Alps across the lake. Runs 14 May to 1 November, 08:20 to 17:00 on a weekday.

weather_swaps.instead_of: A washed-out day in the valley
weather_swaps.do: Blausee. Fifty minutes each way from Grindelwald down the Kandertal, a forest lake that still works in drizzle, with a 300 m paved loop and a glass-bottomed rowing boat in the price.

booking_order: Grindelwald apartment, 6-9 September. Still the tightest item, but these dates sit before the Eidgenössisches Jugendjodelfest rather than inside it, so the village is not booked out around you. Three bedrooms sleeping five, with an included parking space.
Weggis, 10-11 September. Ask whether parking is included; it is CHF 13 a day if not.

Allegra Lodge, Kloten. The two-bedroom suite for 4-6 September, plus one single room for the night of the 5th once the fifth traveller is here, plus one family room for the 12th. Take the free-cancellation rates and tell them the flight lands at 20:30.

Confirm the van for a Sunday 6 September morning collection and a Saturday 12 September evening return, and add a second driver. Six days - ask whether a full week costs less anyway. Check height against 2.30 m.
Five Half Fare Cards, covering 4-13 September.
Jungfraujoch seat reservations, once the forecast is clear.
Piz Gloria brunch for five, Wednesday. The table reservation is required.
Nothing at all for the Saturday. The Knabenschiessen is free to enter and Zurich's old town needs no ticket.
Nothing else. Rigi, Lungern, Männlichen, Schilthorn, Pfingstegg and the Aare Gorge are all walk-up.

totals.note_vs_six: At six the shared costs barely move - the Grindelwald apartment, the van and the airport rooms at each end cost much the same either way - so the total would rise by about one more person's tickets and food while the figure each fell. Five costs less overall but more each. At six the luggage would not have fitted.
